==English== {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alter|en|neest||dialectal}} * {{alter|en|neist||Scotland}} * {{alter|en|nex||archaic}} * {{alter|en|nex'||dialectal}} ===Etymology=== From {{inh|en|enm|nexte}}, {{m|enm|nexste}}, {{m|enm|nixte}}, from {{inh|en|ang|nīehsta}}, {{m|ang|nīehste}}, etc., inflected forms of {{m|ang|nīehst|t=nearest, next}}, superlative form of {{m|ang|nēah||nigh}} (the comparative would become {{m|en|near}}), corresponding to {{inh|en|gem-pro|*nēhwist|t=nearest, closest}}; equivalent to {{suffix|en|nigh|est|nocat=1}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|naist|t=next}}, {{cog|nl|naast|t=next to}}, {{cog|de|nächster|t=next}}, {{cog|yi|נעקסט|t=next}}, {{cog|da|næste|t=next}}, {{cog|ovd|nest|t=by, near}}, {{cog|is|næst|t=next}}, {{cog|nb,nn|neste|t=next}}, {{cog|sv|näst}}, {{m|sv|nästa|t=next}}, {{cog|fa|نزد|tr=nazd|t=near, with}}. Compare typologically {{m+|la|proximus||nearest, next}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|nĕkst}}, {{IPA|en|/nɛkst/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-next.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-next.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛkst|s=1}} ===Adjective=== {{en-adj|-}} # {{l|en|nearest|Nearest}} in place or position, having nothing similar intervening; {{l|en|adjoining}}. #: {{ux|en|The man in the '''next''' bunk kept me awake all night with his snoring.}} #: {{ux|en|She lives a mile or two away, in the '''next''' village.}} #: {{ux|en|I live in the '''next''' house to the Grand Hotel.}} #* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=8|passage=Philander went into the '''next''' room, which was just a lean-to hitched on to the end of the shanty, and came back with a salt mackerel that dripped brine like a rainstorm.}} ## {{lb|en|obsolete}} Most direct, or shortest or nearest in distance or time. ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare All's Well|text=A prophet I, Madam; and I speak the truth the '''next''' way: {{...}}}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1777|author=Francis Quarles|title=Emblems Divine and Moral: Together with Hieroglyphics of the Life of Man|section=page 152, epigram 2 |passage=The road to resolution, lies by doubt:
"The '''next''' way home's the farthest way about."}} # Nearest in order, succession, or rank; immediately {{l|en|following}} (or sometimes {{l|en|preceding}}) in order. #: {{ux|en|Please turn to the '''next''' page.}} #: {{ux|en|On Wednesday '''next''', I'm going to Spain.}} #: {{ux|en|the '''next''' chapter; the '''next''' week; the Sunday '''next''' before Easter}} #: {{ux|en|The man was driven by his love for money and his desire to become the '''next''' Bill Gates.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|journal=Yank: the army weekly|volume=4|page=96|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mxYiAQAAMAAJ|year=1945|passage="{{...}}You patriotic?" / "I guess so, as much as the '''next''' guy," I said, wondering how the hell I could shake him.}} # {{lb|en|chiefly|law}} [[nearest|Nearest]] in [[relationship]]. {{q|See also {{m|en|next of kin}}.}} #: ''[[next friend|'''next''' friend]]'' #* {{quote-book|en|year=1793|author=William Peere Williams; Samuel Compton Cox|title=Reports of Cases Argued and Determined in the High Court of Chancery, and of Some Special Cases Adjudged in the Court of King's Bench [1695-1735]: De Term. S. Trin. 1731|page=602 |passage=''Thomas Humphrey Doleman'' died the 30th of ''August'' 1712, an infant, intestate and without issue; ''Lewis'' the '''next''' nephew died the 17th of ''April'' 1716, an infant about sixteen years old, having left his mother ''Mary Webb'', ...}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1874|author=Thomas Sergeant; William Rawle|title=Reports of Cases Adjudged in the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania|page=23 |passage=If it be a property, it is a new species, unknown to the civil law, the common law, and the statute law; there is no medium, it must be, if it goes to her '''next''' kin, because it is absolute property in her. There can be no distribution of personal property ...}} ====Usage notes==== * {{m|en|near|Near}} was originally the [[comparative]] form of {{m|en|nigh}}; the [[superlative]] form was {{m|en|next}}. {{m|en||Nigh}} is used today mostly in archaic, poetic, or regional contexts. ====Synonyms==== * {{sense|nearest in order}} See also [[Thesaurus:former]] or [[Thesaurus:subsequent]] ====Antonyms==== * time to meet.}} #: {{ux|en|I'll know better '''next''' time.}} # {{lb|en|of days of the week or months of the year}} Closest in the [[future]], or closest but one if the closest is very soon; of days, sometimes thought to specifically refer to the instance closest to seven days (one week) in the future. #: {{ux|en|The party is '''next''' Tuesday; that is, not tomorrow, but eight days from now.}} #:
